observation.visible_scene: A static optical-bench setup shot from a fixed camera. On the left, a metal clamp/holder (engraved with vertical text) grips the edge of a transparent rectangular plate standing upright on a black perforated optical table. A circular pool of warm light falls on the plate, and within that circle a sharp square region displays a thin-film-style interference pattern of curved rainbow bands (purple, magenta, orange, yellow). On the right sits a black optical mount on a translation stage with an adjustment knob and a white/silver micrometer handle, with a horizontal metal rod passing behind it; a dark board fills the background.
visible_changes: The square outline, the circular illuminated halo, the bright reflection spot on the left edge of the halo, the plate, the metal holder, the right-hand mount, the rod and the table all keep the same pixel positions from the first to the last frame, indicating no object translation, expansion or camera motion.

The colored bands inside the square show only very slight, gradual repositioning/reshaping of their curves across the ~2.7 s excerpt (e.g. the relative width/curvature of the orange and purple bands shifts marginally), consistent with a slowly evolving interference pattern rather than a discrete event.
No onset, contact, disappearance or completion of any action is observed within the segment; the patterned square is already present and remains present throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produces or modulates the interference pattern (stress, thickness variation, vibration, or a changing optical element) is not shown.
The full apparatus and the light source arrangement are outside the frame.
Whether the subtle fringe drift continues, stops, or reverses after the last frame is unknown.
uncertain_details: The fringe 'motion' is extremely small; it could be a real slow drift or partly camera/exposure noise, so it is reported as tentative.
Material identities of the plate and the nature of the colored pattern (interference vs. reflection) are inferred from appearance only.
No camera movement is detectable, but minor sub-pixel shifts cannot be fully excluded.
